subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Genetics and Caffeine Metabolism
description: A 60-second lesson on Genetics and Caffeine Metabolism.

hook.text: A single gene determines whether you're a fast or slow caffeine metabolizer—and it shapes your entire coffee experience.

buildup.text: The CYP1A2 gene controls how quickly your liver breaks down caffeine. Fast metabolizers clear it in 2–3 hours.

discovery.text: Slow metabolizers take 6–10 hours. They feel jittery, anxious, and have disrupted sleep even from morning coffee.

twist.text: About 50% of the population are slow metabolizers. Many don't know it—they just assume coffee makes everyone anxious.

climax.text: Genetic testing can now identify your metabolizer type, helping personalize caffeine intake for optimal effect.

punchline.text: One gene, two speeds, completely different coffee experiences.

quiz.question: What does the CYP1A2 gene determine?
options: How quickly the liver metabolizes caffeine
Whether you like tea or coffee
